title: Jaeger's 4-flow and 8-flow theorems and Seymour's 6-flow theorem
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Jaeger's 4-flow theorem: every finite 4-edge-connected simple graph has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow, i.e. an antisymmetric function on darts with values in {±1, ±2, ±3} that is conserved at every vertex. Also proved: a graph with two edge-disjoint spanning trees has its edges covered by two even subgraphs (a nowhere-zero ℤ₂ × ℤ₂-flow) and has a nowhere-zero integer 4-flow. Version 2 adds Jaeger's 8-flow theorem: every finite bridgeless graph has its edges covered by three even subgraphs and has a nowhere-zero integer 8-flow; conversely a graph with a nowhere-zero flow has no bridge. Version 3 adds Seymour's 6-flow theorem (every finite bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero integer 6-flow) and Tutte's theorem relating group and integer flows (for k > 0, every nowhere-zero ℤ/k-flow φ lifts to a nowhere-zero integer k-flow ψ with ψ ≡ φ mod k, and conversely an integer k-flow reduces modulo k to a nowhere-zero ℤ/k-flow). Mathlib has no flows.
